subtype: Approach: emotion-aware planning of the first weeks [Thinking]
passage: Lalremsiami, you asked how I got through the first weeks, so I'm Reena, and here is what I did. On the second night I sat on the floor and said out loud: these weeks will be heavy. That's normal. I won't fight it, I'll plan around it. I made a small list on the fridge. Go to class, even if I sit at the back. Eat three times, even if it's toast. Sleep by eleven, phone in the other room. And one rule: no big decisions on days when I'm crying. No changing courses, no messages to him, no cutting my hair. I wrote "ask again in two weeks" beside each idea. Some days I only managed the toast. But the list held the shape of the day while I could not.

qa.q: What time did Reena set for going to sleep?
What was Reena feeling on the second night?
qa.a: Reena felt heavy and sad but accepting, saying the weeks would be hard and choosing to plan around them.

qa.a: Reena could tell one close friend about the list so that someone checks in, because routines are easier to keep when another person knows about them.

qa.a: Lalremsiami asked how Reena managed and receives a plain list, so Lalremsiami can see that getting through was about small steady steps and not a big recovery.

grounding: Shows planning around expected heavy weeks after a breakup by keeping classes, meals and sleep steady and postponing large choices.
